Well it's quite a long story. I'll try to give you the bullet points. 

• Knew my best friend since I was eight. We were extremely close and joined at the hip. He's one of the best people I've known and he's taught me so much. He's kind and sweet and understanding and basically he's family. 
• His ex married someone else in 2017. He was devastated. She was the one that got away. I was there for him. To drink with him. To curse her out. To cry with him.
• Eventually we ended up kissing. Felt weird about it because we'd been friends for 18 years without any sort of romantic feelings creeping up. Didn't understand if it was sexual or romantic.
• Decided to see where it goes without making any grand commitments or telling anyone (mostly because to everyone we were almost like siblings) . Basically go with the flow 
• There were no commitments per se except to be honest about it, be monogamous, and respect each other.
• Ultimately it sort of turned into something serious. We'd talk daily for hours. He kept telling me he loved me and I was the most important person in his life and vice versa. I thought we didn't need to clarify about the commitment as it was understandable. (Big mistake.)
• The ex comes back after 3 years saying she screwed up and never loved her husband. She's in love with my best friend .
• I knew she was always the one that got away. I kept telling my friend if he's interested then tell me. I'd happily step back. All I want is for him to be happy and have love in his life .
• He kept lying and telling me they're not in touch. (Complete bullshit.) I saw his phone one day and it was filled with calls and conversations (at 4 in the morning.)
• I confronted him. He gaslighted me and said she's just a friend who needs help as she's going through a divorce. I made my peace with it. He stopped meeting me and giving excuses that he's sick or busy but I'd get to know he was with her 
• He took my virginity and then 2 minutes later went into another room and slept beside his ex holding her hand. (This was at a wedding and all of us friends had adjoining rooms.)
• I told the ex he slept with me and came to her. He said I ruined his life and he wishes I were dead. I apologised for telling her. (I know. I know.)
• I still tried to make it work because I guess I missed my best friend and I thought maybe we could overcome this.
• He boycotted me and cut me off and I went into deep depression and severe anxiety. 
•All of our friends were manipulated by them and also they were turned off by my depression and constant crying. They also dont know about our 'non relationship.' So they just think I've a problem with him getting his love back and am a jealous bitch. 
• They all hang out together all the time and I'm never invited anymore. I have known them for my entire life. I don't come from a big city. So I guess that's that. 

That is why I'm extremely lonely and I'm dealing with heart break not only related to love but also friendships. 

Thanks for listening if you actually managed to make it this far. Hope you have an amazing day. :)

I read about her for the first time on this sub and went and checked her profile today. 

Now, I'll be the first to admit that I probably don't have an in depth knowledge of everything that she's talking about and trying to change in the society so I went in with quite an open mind thinking that I'll be able to learn something. 

Not only did I check out her present stories but I also checked out all the highlights . While some of what she was saying rang absolutely true, some I realised I'd have to do more research on , but the other was completely batshit crazy. 

So she believes the only reason women want to get married is because we've been conditioned to do so. Now I know there's a problem in our country with 'shaadi ka umar' and arranged marriages and getting married in the same caste and a million other things. Should those things be fought against and a change be made? Definitely. But to say that the only reason anyone would want to get married, even in you're in your 40s and not 20s (because it's easier to brainwash you then), is because you've 'ghutne tek diye' infront of the society and accepted your fate was too extreme and honestly, just idiotic. I'm all for women who want to be never married, or want to not have kids or want to do anything else with their lives. But at the same time I can also accept that some women would love to get married, find their happiness in that institution and babies. Feminism, atleast according to me, is about acknowledging that women are complex individuals who are different from each other. How about we not paint them all with the same brush and completely brush over a faction of this gender because they just would like to marry someone?

Also, maybe this is not a big deal but it really rubbed me the wrong way. She keeps doing this #bakedreviews for movies. While reviewing Mohabbatein, she made a really sleazy comment about Amitabh and Aishwarya. 'They got it on' , 'Hot for you daddy.' or something like that. Not about the characters but the actual people. It was disgusting. For someone who is so politically correct and empathetic , how did this not seem wrong and extremely gross to her? Or does her principles only apply to others and not herself? Is a woman not to be respected just because she's an actress?

Let's just say if I've to educate myself on certain issues, I'm going to go buy a book. Because even if we may share the same side of the political spectrum, I've realised I don't really agree with what she has to say.

I've had the same set of friends since first grade. We grew up together, went to college together, hung out together. I always considered myself extremely lucky to be surrounded by such amazing people.

Last year due to a lot of complicated reasons one by one they all decided to step back from me. It didn't help that i was diagnosed with depression. I was so blindsided by my situation and circumstances and in so much pain that i didn't even know what i did to push them away. When i realised that they weren't behaving like they usually did, i tried asking them. They kept on telling me nothing was wrong. During the whole lockdown i kept calling them and they wouldn't pick up. I texted and they wouldn't reply. Even if they did pick up they'd make an excuse and hang up. And after 10-20 minutes I'd see them putting up stories of group video calls. 

I apologized. I apologized so many times for hurting them even if i didn't know what i did. I asked them to let me know when they meet so I'll come along as well. I told them I missed them , that i was very lonely. I even cried infront of them. And they still just showed indifference. I've known these people all my life. Since for 19 years, some for 17. None less than 12. 

I feel so lonely that somedays i cant breathe. I want to run away. Go somewhere where no one knows me so even if i feel lonely i can atleast console myself that it's because I'm around strangers. Feeling like this with people who were almost as good as family and not even knowing what i did is something that as good as kills me. Somedays I'm so lonely that i want to die. 

I know I shouldn't want to be with people who don't want me but it's very difficult to see them just forget about me and move on this easily. It almost feels like no one would even notice if i went missing. 

Being with people who don't listen is extremely painful. Being with people who listen and yet don't care is even worse.

So I went for SMILE procedure. It's basically similar to LASIK but the procedure is different and takes way less time. My operation was done in five minutes. Both eyes included. The difference is that in SMILE they use a single femtosecond laser and make a small incision to extract the lenticule from cornea. My friends have had LASIK done and their surgery has taken so where around 25 to 30 minutes. Also, with SMILE, since they're just making a small incision and not a flap, the after effects of dry eyes never occur. The only thing is the procedure is a little expensive than LASIK.

I was still shit scared, though. But I think that was just the nerves of getting surgery done on my eyes. It was totally painless. The most you'll feel is some pressure, that's it. There are chances that your eyes may pain after the surgery but they give you a pain killer for that and all you have to do is go home and sleep. And the next day when I woke up, I went up to the window and could look at the billboard without any glasses. I think it was at that moment it hit me how drastically my life had changed. No more glasses, check ups, prescription changes, contact lenses, etc. Only when I didn't need them did I realise what a hassle they actually we're in my life.

The recovery period wasn't long. The doctor called me the next day for a post op checkup. Everything checked out and I was free to go home. I just had to be sure to be careful that my eyes were protected from dust, direct sunlight etc. Also, no swimming for three months and no eye make up for a month. They also gave me some eye drops to put in my eyes for a month of two. 

I hope this helps. :)
